Tabs and shells = 
Each tab is a real terminal: PowerShell, Command Prompt, WSL (Linux), Git Bash or the built-in Lisp. The + opens the default shell, the arrow next to it lets you choose. When you reopen CorbolPrompt the tabs come back, in their folders. Right-click the terminal to copy, paste and ask the assistant. = 
The assistant = 
On the right there is the AI assistant: ask it for a command or to explain an error. It sees the shell, the folder and the last lines of the screen. The commands it suggests become ▶ buttons: you run them, with a click, only if you want. Choose the service (Claude Code, API, local assistant) at the top of the panel. = 
Save the commands you use often: select them in the terminal, right click → Add to favorites, or right-click a command from the assistant (the description writes itself). Below the terminal you see the favorites for the shell you are using: click to run, Shift+click to paste. = 
Lisp = 
The Lisp tab is a small Common Lisp: defun, loop, format, numbers as big as you like, and system commands like (sh "dir"), (cd "..") and (ls). Arrows for history, Tab to complete, Ctrl+C to interrupt. Type (help) for a summary; the assistant knows this dialect. =
